name: Jaddua
overview: Jaddua was a male member of the tribe of Levi known primarily as the son of Jonathan, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:11. Beyond this unique familial identification, little additional information or notes are provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaddua means 'one known,' a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 12:11. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it serves as a personal identifier within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jaddua as the son of Jonathan, based on Nehemiah 12:11. No other family relationships are recorded, and thus his lineage is noted only in connection to his father.
scriptureSignificance: Jaddua's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his identification as a Levite and descendant of Jonathan, situating him within the priestly or Levitical lineage important for temple service and worship. His mention in Nehemiah 12:11 places him in the genealogical context significant for understanding the restoration period after the exile, highlighting the continuity of the Levitical line.
